summary: The root "bsm" primarily means "to smile," a gentle, soundless laugh, less intense than full laughter.
lane: 5 تبسّم بسم تبسم ; and ; and , aor. بَسِمَ inf. n. بَسْمٌ (S, M, Msb, K) and مَبْسَمٌ ; (K, * TA;) [ He smiled; ] these verbs signify less than ضَحِكَ [so that they are properly explained by the Latin subrisit ]: (S, Msb:) or he opened his lips like him who displays to another his teeth: (Lth, TA:) or he laughed in the least degree and in the most beautiful manner: (M, K:) or he laughed a little without any sound: (Msb:) or تَبَسُّمٌ is the beginning of ضَحِكٌ [or laughter ]: (Towsheeh, and Neseem er-Riyád, in TA art. ضحك , q. v.:) accord. to Zj, it is the utmost degree of laughing of the prophets. (M.) -b2- [Hence,] السَّحَابُ عَنِ البَرْقِ (M,) or تبسّم عَنْهُ (TA,) i. q. اِنْكَلَّ عنه [i. e. (tropical:) The clouds displayed a faint flashing of lightning ]. (M, TA.) -b3- And تبسّم الطَّلْعُ (tropical:) The extremities of the طلع [i. e. the spadix, or the spathe, of the palm-tree, ] burst asunder. (TA.)

headwords.def: بَسَمَ بسم بٱسم سم: see 5, with which it is syn. [Hence,] مَا بَسَمْتُ فِى الشَّىْءِ (tropical:) I did not taste the thing. (K, TA.)

بَسَّامٌ بسام سام سامي (S M, K) and (S, K) epithets from بَسَمَ, (M, K,) applied to a man, (S, M,) meaning كَثِيرُ التَّبَسُّمِ [ That smiles much ]. (S.)
بَاسِمٌ باسم بٱسم ٱسم part. n. of بَسَمَ [meaning Smiling ]. (K, TA.)

مَبْسِمٌ مبسم i. q. ثَغْرٌ (S, K,) meaning The front teeth: (TK:) [and sometimes, perhaps, the mouth: ] so called as being the place of التَّبَسُّم [or smiling: pl. مَبَاسِمُ ]. (TA.) One says, [of women or girls,] هُنَّ غُرُّ المَبَاسِمِ [ They are white in the front teeth ]. (TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
